claim_rows.label: Soundness
claim_rows.level: a bound, q/2^124 + 2^-101, proved in Lean for exact match
claim_rows.text: The protocol's soundness is proved in Lean 4. A provider that tries to pass off output that is not the committed model's is caught, except with probability about q/2^124 + 2^-101 after q hash queries.

claim_rows.label: Assumptions
claim_rows.level: listed, with the security model: random oracle, classical adversaries
claim_rows.text: The client must trust what no call checks: the commitment ID, the expected policy and its numbers, the tokenizer and chat template, and `cp_verify` itself.

claim_rows.label: Weakening switches
claim_rows.level: test switches listed; a production build that sets a listed one does not compile; the list sees only macros defined before it
claim_rows.note: Our note: the clipped-gap acceptance policy was read and not copied into this slot: FlashProve calls it the expected use and does not call it a switch that weakens the check. What an accepting check under it says is quoted under What a passing check shows and What the proof leaves open.
claim_rows.text: Tests' own switches are another kind (`fence.h` lists them): some of them let a test disable checks, choose the private randomness or call functions that only a test may call; one keeps what the library's prover sends out of its own hash chain, for tests of hiding.

claim_rows.label: What stays open
claim_rows.level: listed: the provider chooses the model, and more
claim_rows.text: The provider chooses the model. A yes does not say whose weights they are, that the shipped committer made the commitment, or which real model it is.

claim_rows.label: Soundness
claim_rows.level: 100 conjectured bits, in a source code comment
claim_rows.note: Our note: this is a comment in the prover's source, not a documentation page. The documentation names the security block only as "`security` (the FRI parameters and the hash)" (prover/README.md L324) and states no security notion in words.
claim_rows.text:
stwo's own conjectured-soundness accounting is
    security_bits = pow_bits + log_blowup_factor * n_queries
so blowup 2 (log_blowup_factor = 1) at 100 conjectured bits means exactly
100 FRI queries and no grinding.

claim_rows.label: Assumptions
claim_rows.note: Our note: SASH uses "assumption" only for cost-model inputs, never for what a proof rests on. Passages that name what the verifier takes as input were not copied here, because calling them assumptions would be our inference: `boundary-grid --verify` demands the calibration manifest and `--prompt` (prover/README.md L49-L52), and the model root "stays a comparison against the same manifest" (prover/README.md L56-L59). The source comment under the security notion speaks of "conjectured" soundness.

claim_rows.label: Weakening switches
claim_rows.level: --unsound-skip-* documented; flagged in every proof; the results repository refuses to tag a release that cites one
claim_rows.text: Every skip flag names one of these edges, and `--unsound-argmax-lax` weakens edge 16 rather than dropping it. A run whose `provenance.unsound_skips` is not empty is a control or a measurement of cost, never a statement about a forward pass, and `zk-results` refuses to tag a release that cites one.

claim_rows.label: What stays open
claim_rows.level: listed: both ends of a request are outside every proof, and more
claim_rows.text: Both ends of a request -- the text in and the text out -- are outside every proof this repository records.

security_notion.text:
stwo's own conjectured-soundness accounting is
    security_bits = pow_bits + log_blowup_factor * n_queries
so blowup 2 (log_blowup_factor = 1) at 100 conjectured bits means exactly
100 FRI queries and no grinding.

glyph.label: Draft criteria, prototype only, needs an RFC (RFC-0001)

properties.amber: Hidden with a stated limit: a named leak, hiding shown only for one policy or setting, or hiding optional per circuit.
properties.green: The documentation says the weights stay hidden from the checker in the default use, naming no leak beyond public settings.
properties.grey: No statement about hiding the weights from the checker (hiding from a host operator is another property), or not copied yet.
properties.name: Weights hidden
properties.not_here: Hiding from the host operator (an enclave) is not this property.
properties.question: Does the checker learn nothing about the weights?
properties.red: The documentation says the checker sees the weights or hiding is off, or the design gives the checker the weights.

properties.amber: Tied with a stated limit: only under one of several policies, within a tolerance or bound, or shown only in empirical tests.
properties.green: The documentation says a passing check ties each checked token to the committed weights exactly, in the default or expected use.
properties.grey: Not stated, or not copied yet.
properties.name: Model bound
properties.not_here: Which real, named model the commitment is: FlashProve and SASH both say that stays outside their proof; it is printed as text beside the glyph, not coloured.
properties.question: Is each checked token tied to the committed weights?
properties.red: The documentation says outputs are not tied to any weights, or nothing is checked.

properties.amber: One check covers a stated part: the positions the client names, one segment, or one disputed step.
properties.green: The documentation says one check, or one joined set of checks, covers the prompt and every output token of a request.
properties.grey: Not stated (for example a graph run whose output tokens are not named), or not copied yet.
properties.name: Whole output proved
properties.not_here: Which requests get a proof (sampling, post-hoc proving) is a deployment choice, not what one check covers. The text before tokenizing and after detokenizing: FlashProve and SASH both say it is outside their proof; printed as text.
properties.question: Does one check cover every output token of a request?
properties.red: The documentation says no output token is checked, or nothing is checked.

properties.amber: Machine-checked for a stated part only: one component, or a weaker statement than the one the system makes.
properties.green: The documentation says the protocol's soundness is proved in a proof assistant (Lean, Coq, Isabelle or similar).
properties.grey: Not stated, or not copied yet.
properties.name: Formally verified
properties.not_here: Whether the programs users run are proved: no row claims it; it is printed as text.
properties.question: Is the security argument checked by a proof assistant?
properties.red: The documentation says it is not machine-checked: planned only, or the evidence named is review and tests.

properties.amber: A numeric level is stated but called conjectured, or stated only in code or configuration, or for part of the system.
properties.green: The documentation states a numeric soundness bound and says it is proven, by hand or by machine, under named assumptions.
properties.grey: No level stated, or not copied yet.
properties.name: Security level
properties.not_here: The number itself is a quote in its card; the glyph shows only whether one is stated and proven. The level is judged for the protocol, as the documentation states it; whether the programs a checker runs meet it is printed as text beside the segment (no row proves its programs).
properties.question: Is a soundness level stated, and proven?
properties.red: The documentation says the settings give no meaningful soundness, for example a test-only setting.

properties.amber: The documentation states a trusted input or condition that its proved statement does not cover: a setup file, public files the user must grant were fixed before the hash (a provider who tuned them is outside the statement), or one honest party among several.
properties.green: The documentation says a check rests on cryptography alone or needs no trusted setup, and names no chip or party to trust.
properties.grey: Not stated, or not copied yet.
properties.name: No trusted party
properties.not_here: Trust every row shares is not counted: the checker's own computer, compiler and verifier build, and where the commitment or the weights come from (see Model bound).
properties.question: Does a check hold without trusting a chip maker, a setup ceremony or an honest party?
properties.red: The check is a hardware attestation verified against a chip maker's keys, or nothing is checked and the provider is trusted.

risks.fix: Not stated is an empty slice, labelled 'not stated', never 'no'. Public-source rows sit on their own tab with 'from public sources, limits not copied' and are never set in the same table as card rows. Before a public-source row sits beside a benchmarked row, copy its claim card. Optional switch for the RFC: cap public-source rows at amber.
risks.what: Thoroughness penalty. FlashProve states its limits at length and collects amber; SASH's silence at the pin gives grey; rows from one public sentence can show green (Attestable: four green from one blog post). A reader may think the less documented system covers more.

risks.fix: Owner decision for the RFC: may a system's own dated publication outside the pin set a colour? Until then the slice stays empty with no mark; pointing at it, the card and the system page print the note with its quote, and ask SASH to state it in the repository.
risks.what: Pin rule for SASH. Its own research note (outside the pin) says the proofs are not yet zero knowledge and that its soundness evidence is human review and negative controls. Counted, SASH would read amber for Weights hidden and red for Formally verified; at the pin both are grey, which a FlashProve reader may call favourable to SASH.

risks.fix: Colour per benchmark configuration once the FlashProve policy mapping (issue #69) is fixed.
risks.what: FlashProve Model bound is amber because its expected use is the clipped-gap policy; exact match, which FlashProve also ships and proves, would be green.

risks.fix: Kept: the criteria differ (a hand-proved bound is green for Security level and not for Formally verified). Say so on the reading page.
risks.what: FlashProve's Formally verified and Security level are both green from the same Lean work: one fact, two segments.

risks.fix: None: the word is SASH's own and the reason quotes it.
risks.what: SASH Security level is amber for 'conjectured' FRI soundness, the usual accounting of STARK systems.

risks.fix: Round 7 applies option (b): the amber criterion names a condition the documentation puts outside its proved statement, and the shared-caveat rule says when fixed parameters count. Option (a), a shared caveat printed as text, would turn FlashProve grey or green; owner decision for the RFC. Invite the SASH team to state its assumptions.
risks.what: FlashProve No trusted party is amber for a condition it names ('that you grant'): its public files must be fixed before the hash, and a provider who tuned them is outside the statement. Every non-interactive proof fixes public parameters before the hash (VerInf says its seeds come from sequential Fiat-Shamir), so the FlashProve team may call this a disclosure penalty. SASH's verifier also takes a calibration manifest and model roots as given but does not call them assumptions, so it is grey.

rules: No total, no score, no rank. Segments are never summed, counted or averaged; rows stay A to Z.
Each colour comes from the written criterion above and at least one verbatim quote with its source, except grey, which carries the list of sources read or the words 'not copied yet'.
Never infer. If the sources read are silent, the segment is grey. Not stated is an empty slice with a thin outline: nothing is stated, which is not no, good or bad.

Rows with a claim card (FlashProve, SASH): the state comes from the pinned repositories only. A system's own statement outside the pin is printed as a line under the segment, in the card and on the system page (outside_pin), and does not set the segment's colour.
Rows not benchmarked yet: the state comes from the quotes in landscape.json (public sources, no claim card). Their tab and their pages say 'from public sources, limits not copied'.

Reference rows (RFC-0015) prove nothing (RFC-0015 L45). Both are red on Formally verified and Security level, meaning 'no security argument, by definition', not a fault. Plain serving is red on every segment; Recompute's other segments are coloured from what RFC-0015 says it does. Reference rows are drawn as the same pie and sit on their own tab.
Each stated limit is counted in one segment only (FlashProve's clipped-gap policy: Model bound; its one-bit leak: Weights hidden). A limit counted elsewhere is printed beside the segment (aside).

Caveats every row shares do not change a colour (programs tested, not proved; compilers and hardware of the checker trusted; which real model a commitment is). They are printed as text. Public parameters fixed before the hash are shared by every non-interactive proof; they set amber only where the documentation says its proved statement excludes a provider who tuned them.

Colour is never the only signal: a slice is one flat ink or empty. The three inks step in lightness (No, then Partly, then Yes) and Not stated is empty, so the states still read in grayscale. The state word is always one press away, on the system page, and in the rows on this page.
The first quote of a coloured segment is the one that sets its state; further quotes support it.

green.label: holds
green.meaning: The property holds, per the system's own documentation.

grey.label: not stated
grey.meaning: Not stated in the sources read, or not copied by us yet. Silence is never red.

red.label: does not hold
red.meaning: The system's documentation says it does not hold, or the design rules it out.

glyph.status: draft criteria, prototype only, needs an RFC (RFC-0001)

neither_line.scope: Checked over the passages we copied from each system, not over all of its documentation.
neither_line.show_when: both claim cards are copied and neither states it; decided by the builder from claims
neither_line.text: Neither system's statement says the answer is true, safe or fair. A proof is about which computation produced it.

home.no_division_line: No number on this site is divided by the other system's number. A shared task for both systems is planned for v0.2.
home.setups_h2: Both systems prove that an answer came from a fingerprinted model. They do it on different models, for different amounts of text.
home.setups_lede: So read each against the same model run without a proof, never against the other system.
home.size_caption: Size shows how much text one proof covers. Larger is not better or worse: it is a different task.
home.tamper_legend: Text in cobalt is quoted from the system's own documentation, with a link. Text in black is ours.

trace.caption: Illustration from one tamper test on FlashProve: changing one token of the answer made the check reject it.
trace.lede: Below, one request is traced through FlashProve, on its home setup (Llama 4 Maverick · 1,024-token prompt, the next token · 24 requests per batch · one H100 GPU). The steps and the two verdicts come from the mock record of one run and its tamper test, invented for layout.
mechanism: Who holds what. The provider holds the model's weights and publishes a fingerprint of them before proving. The checker works without the weights.

For each answer, the provider's GPU makes a proof. The proof says the answer came from the fingerprinted model, in the sense each system's own statement gives, which this site quotes on each system page.
The checker holds the proof, the fingerprint, the prompt and the answer. It runs on a computer limited to 8 CPU threads and 32 GiB of memory, no GPU, and says accepted or rejected.
trace.other_system_differs: SASH differs: one proof covers a 4,096-token prompt and 512 generated tokens, 4,608 token positions in all.
trace.rule: the alphabetically first system whose home setup recorded the change-one-answer-token test (C1) as rejected

steps.names: FlashProve calls it the commitment ID; SASH, the model commitment or model root.
steps.weights_digest_words: What we hold instead: a hash of the weight files as downloaded, which only identifies the files. The fingerprint is a different value that each system computes from the weights in its own way, and the checker tests the proof against it.
steps.words: The model's fingerprint, published before proving.
The proof, made on one H100 GPU.

steps.basis: This is the untampered proof, which each tamper test checks first, so a later rejection is not a broken checker.
steps.words: The checker, without a GPU, accepts it.
The same answer with one token changed.

trace.why_words: FlashProve is traced because it comes first in alphabetical order among the systems whose test of changing one answer token is recorded. Where SASH differs follows the trace.

landscape.principle: Three descriptive dimensions, each a filter, none a ranking. Values are ordered by the kind of check, never by merit. A system gets a value only from its own sources; otherwise the value is not_stated, shown as an absence, not a verdict.
rules: Facts come only from each system's own repository, paper, docs or post, quoted with a link; repository links pin a full commit.
Every quote was matched against a downloaded copy of its source by make_landscape.py; repository line ranges are computed, not typed.
No performance numbers. Where a system publishes figures, `upstream_figures.where` links them and `copied_here` is false (AGENTS.md rule 2).
not_stated means the listed sources were read and are silent; it is an absence, not a verdict (AGENTS.md rule 9).
Fields named note, ours, *_note and covers_note are our words and must render as ours.
Model sizes appear only as the system names them (model id or stated parameter count).

findings.text: RFC-0004 §Mapping maps SASH `commit` to the harness `commit` scope as exact; SASH's `commit` is the polynomial commitment inside proving (`constants.json` `_timing_scopes.commit`). Amendment A6.

The v3 fixture's FlashProve check time (3.120 s per proof, 8 CPUs) is about a fifth of FlashProve's published 16.84 s at 8 threads (FP fig L115). Side by side, the overview would show a discrepancy that no run produced.

SASH publishes its own plain-serving baseline for its shape, vLLM 1341.5898999323858 positions/s end to end, one request at a time (const L4060-L4070). The mock plain-serving row reads 1,347; keep it mock-labelled, and use SASH's figure only in the Published group of the plain-serving row, attributed "published by SASH, not by vLLM".
FlashProve publishes no plain-serving rate, only multiples against stock vLLM 0.29.0 serving the FP8 release on eight H100s (`docs/limits-all-rows.tsv` L1382).

The post says the hash-based compile "offers even post-quantum security"; the repository at the pin states "against classical adversaries" (`guide/what-is-proved.md` L57-L58). Claims follow the pinned repository (rule 9), so the card says classical.
SASH's headline manifest records `"prover_dirty": true` (L475). Its published figures stay `reported` under INV-TIER-4 whoever reruns them.
The SASH claim class has two defensible `<output>` tokens (`greedy-continuation`, `segment-grid`). Ask the SASH team before any class filter ships.
RFC-0015 says nothing about the text ends (tokenizer, chat template, detokenisation) for recompute; the chain draws them `not stated`. One line in RFC-0015 would settle it.

method_changes.not_proposed: per-axis "leaderboards" that each open sorted by their own value. That makes every performance column a default order, which S5 and PRD §5 ("Ranking systems or naming a 'fastest' or 'best' prover") forbid by design; the alternative a reader gets in one click is the same list. If the owner wants it anyway, it is a PRD §5 change, not an RFC-0009 edit.
